blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A good ending matters as much as a good start. Today we say goodbye to London. We finish the UK track together.

You learned many polite phrases this track. You can use them every day. You can close a meeting, an email, or a short talk with a warm goodbye.

"Bye" is friendly. "See you soon" is warm. "Take care" fits most moments. Remember: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts. Practice a little every day, even five minutes.

items.q: What does the text say we do today?
options: Say goodbye and finish the UK track
Book a new trip to London
items.why: "Today we say goodbye to London. We finish the UK track together."

items.q: According to the text, where can you use these polite phrases?
options: In a meeting, an email, or a short talk
items.why: "You can close a meeting, an email, or a short talk with a warm goodbye."

items.q: The text says English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts. This suggests the author wants you to…
items.why: Inferência: a frase é um incentivo — foque no que você consegue fazer, não no que não consegue.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: "See you soon" is a warm goodbye.
Five minutes a day is a good habit.
How you finish does not matter.
items.why: Inferência: o texto abre dizendo que o final importa tanto quanto o começo.

items.q: "Practice a little every day, even five minutes" suggests that…
options: you should stop after this track
small, regular practice is enough to help
you need many hours each day
items.why: Inferência: pouco e constante é melhor do que nada — o hábito diário conta.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie se despedindo do visitante no último dia em Londres. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi! It is your last day here in London. I am so happy you came to visit us. You worked really hard this week, and your English is much better now. I am proud of you.

Before you go, I want to say a few things. Thank you for your time and your good energy. You were kind to all the team, and we will miss you here at the office.

Remember the polite phrases we practised together. When you leave a meeting, say a clear thank you to the room. When you write an email, always add a sign-off at the end. Short and warm is best.

"Take care" works almost anywhere. "See you soon" keeps it friendly. And when a British friend says "Have a good one," now you know what it means!

Do not stop now. Practice a little every day, even just five minutes on the bus or before bed. Confidence grows with repetition, so keep going. You can do this.

So, safe travels home. Send me a message when you land. Take care, and see you soon. Cheers!
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What day is it in the audio?
options: The visitor's last day in London
A normal day at the office
items.why: "It is your last day in London."

items.q: What does Sophie say about writing emails?
options: Send emails only in the morning
Always add a sign-off at the end
items.why: "When you write an email, always add a sign-off at the end."

items.q: How does Sophie feel about the visitor?
options: She is worried about the office
She is happy and proud of the progress
items.why: Inferência: ela diz que está feliz, que vão sentir falta e que o inglês melhorou — um tom caloroso.

items.q: Why does Sophie say "Do not stop now"?
options: Because the meeting is not over
Because the team needs more emails
Because she wants the visitor to keep practising after leaving
items.why: Inferência: ela liga a frase a "practice every day" — é um pedido para continuar estudando.

items.q: What does "safe travels" mean here?
items.why: Safe travels = boa viagem, dito para quem vai partir.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Take care, and call me when you arrive." Take care means…
items.why: Take care = cuide-se; uma despedida calorosa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "You are leaving tomorrow? ___ home!"
items.why: Safe travels = boa viagem, dito para quem vai partir.

items.q: "Thanks for the coffee. Cheers!" In British English, cheers here means…
items.why: Cheers (informal) = obrigado / tchau no inglês britânico.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "I have to go now. ___ soon!"
items.why: See you soon = até mais; uma despedida amigável.

items.q: "She waved and said goodbye." Goodbye is…
options: a word you say when you leave
items.why: Goodbye = tchau; usado ao sair.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs úteis para fechar reuniões e conversas. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's wrap up the meeting." To wrap up means to…
items.why: Wrap up = encerrar, terminar a reunião.

items.q: "I will sign off now. Thanks, everyone." To sign off means to…
items.why: Sign off = encerrar (um e-mail, uma ligação) com uma despedida.

items.q: "Let's catch up next month." To catch up means to…
items.why: Catch up = colocar a conversa em dia, encontrar de novo.

items.q: "Come drop by the office when you are in town." To drop by means to…
items.why: Drop by = dar uma passada rápida, visitar sem hora marcada.

items.q: "The team came to see off the visitor at the door." To see someone off means to…
options: say goodbye to someone who is leaving
items.why: See someone off = acompanhar e se despedir de quem está partindo.
